verdict: NO BENEFIT. Balancing is left OFF in the canonical configuration.
question: ToN-IoT is 1746:3 imbalanced and its rarest training classes have 7 edges. Does GraphSMOTE-style oversampling of minority edge representations lift any rung?

method.technique: GraphSMOTE-style interpolation of minority EDGE REPRESENTATIONS
method.why_embedding_space: Zhao et al. (GraphSMOTE, WSDM 2021) show that interpolating raw attributes on a graph yields out-of-domain samples; interpolation must happen in the encoder's output space. Graph topology is never modified.
method.why_not_knn_smote: Textbook SMOTE needs k_neighbors < n_samples. ToN's rarest training classes have 7 edges, so k=5 nearest-neighbour SMOTE is unreliable-to-invalid. The implementation interpolates between random same-class pairs instead.
method.leakage_control: TRAIN-fold edges only; validation and test are never augmented.
method.class_weights: Recomputed on the BALANCED distribution. Keeping the original inverse-frequency weights on top of an oversampled batch corrects the same imbalance twice: observed AGAF collapse to 0.0227 macro-F1, predicting xss 1121 times against 12 true instances and zero Benign. See splits.class_weights_from_labels.
method.prior_art_on_these_datasets: LGSMOTE-IDS (Expert Systems with Applications, 2025) reports large minority-class gains with weighted-distance SMOTE on NF-UNSW-NB15, NF-BoT-IoT and NF-ToN-IoT. We do not reproduce a benefit on the AGGREGATED ToN graph.

seed_verified_comparison.note: 0.05 was the single-seed apparent optimum; three seeds were run to test it.

llm.note: The prototype scorer fits no parameters and averages each class's embeddings; interpolating between same-class points cannot move that average. Unchanged to 4 decimals at every ratio, as predicted.

findings: BALANCING DOES NOT HELP THE GNN. The single-seed result (+0.0535 at ratio 0.05) did not survive: across three seeds the effect is +0.0132 with a seed sd of ~0.020, i.e. inside the noise band. An earlier reading of this sweep called the GNN the new best rung; that was a single-seed artifact and is retracted.

BALANCING CLEARLY HURTS AGAF: -0.0730 across three seeds (0.4341 -> 0.3611), several times the off-balancing seed sd of 0.0113. It also nearly quadruples AGAF's variance (sd 0.0113 -> 0.0434), so balanced AGAF is both worse and less stable.
The loop is unaffected (-0.0028, inside noise) and the LLM rung is exactly unchanged.
AGAF WITHOUT BALANCING REMAINS THE BEST RUNG (0.4341 +/- 0.0113 across seeds). No balancing ratio in 0.05-0.50 produces a configuration that beats it.

Seed variance on this graph is substantial (GNN sd ~0.021, AGAF sd ~0.011 unbalanced). The canonical single-seed contract values are point estimates with that much noise around them, and single-seed comparisons on ToN should not be trusted.
decision: Balancing stays OFF (--oversample-ratio 0.0, the default) in the canonical configuration on every dataset. The flag is retained so the negative result is reproducible, and it is verified inert at 0.0: the full pipeline reproduces the Phase 1 ladder exactly (0.3271 / 0.2785 / 0.4447 / 0.3876).
